selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What did the traveller believe is the main purpose of life in this world?
questions.answer: Faith.

questions.question: Which book did he call the one spoken by the Being he was seeking?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: Which book did he choose to study?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: Because he lived in the present age, what did he look at first?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: How are the many parts of the Risale-i Nur explained in the passage?
questions.answer: As shining points and solid explanations taken from the Qur’an.

questions.question: What is the Risale-i Nur trying to spread?
questions.answer: The truths of the Qur’an.

questions.question: What does that show about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: That it is the source and authority behind it, and that it is from heaven, not from people.

questions.question: Did the traveller deny that there are many proofs?
questions.answer: No. He said there are many, and he would only point to a few.

questions.question: Which two writings are named for giving a strong proof of the Qur’an’s wonder?
questions.answer: The Twenty-Fifth Word and the end of the Nineteenth Letter.

questions.question: How is the traveller described at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: He is hard-working, never satisfied, and always searching.

questions.question: What three praising ideas are said about the Qur’an near the start?
questions.answer: It is very well-known, very bright, and very wise.

questions.question: What holy book did he plan to examine?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the Qur’an do in every age?
questions.answer: It challenges those who refuse to accept it.

questions.question: What is said about the contents of its many parts?
questions.answer: They come from the Qur’an and explain it well.

questions.question: What book did he use first to help with that question?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What does the passage say no one can do to the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: No one can overcome it.

questions.question: What do the proof sections named in the passage help show?
questions.answer: They help show many signs of the Qur’an’s miraculous nature.

questions.question: What is shown by the proof in the two named parts of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: Many signs that the Qur’an is miraculous.

questions.question: What truth about life had the traveller already learned?
questions.answer: That faith is the aim and true life of a person.

questions.question: To what part of himself did he speak?
questions.answer: His heart.

questions.question: What did he say must be known first about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: That it comes from our Creator.

questions.question: Why did he turn first to the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: Because he was living in this time.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the Risale-i Nur built from?
questions.answer: Clear lights and explanations from the Qur’an.

questions.question: What happens to the Risale-i Nur in that difficult age?
questions.answer: People cannot defeat it.
